1. Pension Credit (Guarantee Credit)
Rules: PC-1: Claimant must live in England, Scotland, or Wales and have reached State Pension age. PC-2: Claimant must include partner; both partners must have reached State Pension age (simplified). PC-3: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; above that, every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income. PC-4: Guarantee Credit tops up weekly income to £238 (single) or £363.25 (couple); eligible if assessed income below threshold. PC-5: Weekly Guarantee Credit amount is the difference between the threshold and assessed weekly income.

Facts: She is 61, state pension age 67. She has NOT reached state pension age. So PC-1 fails. Therefore not eligible. Also she has no partner. Savings £148 < £10,000, so no income from savings. Weekly income £159.61. But age is the main barrier.

CTR-4: People who get Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get maximum reduction (100%). CTR-5: Otherwise, people with capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction. CTR-6: Otherwise, weekly reduction is weekly net council tax charge (annual net charge / 52), less 20% of any weekly income above the applicable amount. Applicable amount is Pension Credit guarantee amount (£238 single, £363.25 couple). Income from savings follows PC rule (£1 a week for every £500 over £10,000). Household eligible if weekly reduction > 0.
